observed_evidence.base_runtime_identity: DEPLOYMENT_MANIFEST.runtime_sha256 identifies the sealed 0.6.76 hosted-staging tarball.
observed_evidence.post_artifact_composition: The Dockerfile adds security/runtime modules and composes ux-overlay content into served CSS/JS after the sealed runtime artifact is verified.
observed_evidence.runtime_admission_before_this_change: PR #59 compares WFM_RUNTIME_SHA256 only with the sealed base runtime artifact identity.
observed_evidence.railway_source_watch: The current customer-proof Railway service watches Dockerfile, DEPLOYMENT_MANIFEST.json, STAGING_FREEZE.json and artifact/** but not security/runtime/** or ux-overlay/**.
observed_evidence.active_runtime_impact: No customer-proof outage or compromise was observed. GitHub autodeploy is disabled and the latest customer-proof Railway deployment remains successful.

causal_timeline.learning: A prior control review already identified that Railway source watch patterns omit security/runtime/** and ux-overlay/**.
A strong fail-closed comparison was added for the sealed base runtime SHA, but its identity boundary stopped at the tarball.
Comparing Docker composition, PR #59 admission logic and Railway watch patterns showed that materially different final application content could retain the same WFM_RUNTIME_SHA256.

inferred_root_cause: Deployment identity was modeled at the immutable base-artifact boundary while the actual deployable application is a composition of that artifact plus security and UX overlays. Source-watch policy and runtime-admission policy therefore shared the same incomplete provenance boundary.

reproduction.method: Modify a UX overlay while leaving the sealed tarball and DEPLOYMENT_MANIFEST.runtime_sha256 unchanged, rebuild the image, and compare the composed application digest.
reproduction.result: The deterministic chaos fixture proves the composed deployment digest changes when ux-overlay/ux-reset-cycle9.js changes even though the base runtime artifact identity is unchanged.

layered_identity: Retain WFM_RUNTIME_SHA256 as the immutable sealed-base-runtime identity.
Add a separately computed deployment content digest over the final /app file tree after security and UX composition.
Require independently configured WFM_DEPLOYMENT_SHA256 to equal the image-baked composed digest before server startup.
fixtures: matching base and composed identities clear attestation before the next independent hosted-staging guard
prevention.startup_order: base-runtime attestation -> composed-deployment attestation -> hosted/identity guards -> application server

recovery_rule: Never auto-correct WFM_DEPLOYMENT_SHA256 from source or from the running image after a mismatch. Recovery requires independent verification of the intended composed image followed by an authorized audited configuration update, or rollback to the previously attested deployment.

metrics.mean_detection_effort_direction: reduced: cross-source manual correlation becomes deterministic CI/startup admission
metrics.recovery_path_quality: improved but requires authorized configuration rollout before deployment
metrics.prevention_coverage_change: sealed base artifact only -> sealed base artifact plus final composed application content

open_uncertainty: The current Railway customer-proof service does not yet expose a WFM_DEPLOYMENT_SHA256 variable name, so this prevention must not be deployed until an authorized configuration rollout is coordinated.
The connected Railway OAuth view does not expose plaintext variable values, so current WFM_RUNTIME_SHA256 equality cannot be independently re-read from this automation.

Railway watch patterns still need an authorized infrastructure/configuration change to include security/runtime/** and ux-overlay/**; the runtime attestation reduces but does not replace correct source-watch policy.
